div.p:
Dear Pound: I went to the late Mr Dyer’s funeral this morning but though I shook hands with his widow of course I said nothing except a word of condolence. If you haven’t got the music you will but a month or so of patience perhaps will be needed. I hope you got Michael Kramer
. You may tell Gerhart Hauptmann that he has in me a lifelong admirer – among the thousands of others.

note.p: The face of this postcard shows a photograph of a building, captioned “No 11 Paris - Hôtel de Cluny.” A guidebook of the period stated that the Hôtel de Cluny, in Paris’s Latin Quarter, “is adjoined by the ruins of Roman baths … About 1340 the property came into possession of the Abbey of Cluny (near Mâcon, in Burgundy), and the abbots built their town house here. The present building, an admirable specimen of late-Gothic, under Renaissance influence, was erected by Abbot Jacques d’Amboise between 1485 and 1498, and has since remained almost unaltered” (Karl Baedeker, Paris and its Environs [Leipzig: Karl Baedeker, 1924], 271). The Hôtel de Cluny houses the Musée de Cluny, a vast museum of objects, crafts, and art from the Middle Ages. JJ misaddressed this postcard to Pound at “via Marsala 5, Rapallo.” Pound’s flat was at 12 via Marsala. JJ may have been confused by Pound’s stationery, which read, “Via Marsala. 12-5.” The “5” referred to the fifth floor of the building.

A border of the card carries the credit: “Edition G.-L. Arlaud, Lyon – Juin 1936.” Georges-Louis Arlaud (1869-1944) was a French photographer who had his studio at 3 Place Meissonier in Lyon, France. He produced many high-quality photographs of French, Algerian, Tunisian, and Moroccan scenes and denizens, and he specialized in plein-air nudes and studio portraiture. His images appeared often in magazines and other publications.

div.note: James Dyer (ca. 1860-1938), a wealthy Scottish businessman who had made a fortune in Melbourne, Australia, as an importer of linoleum, married Louise Smith (“his widow”) in 1911. He died on 10 January 1938, and his funeral was the next day. (For additional details, see JJ to Pound, 5 December 1937, notes.)

Louise Berta Mosson Hanson-Dyer, née Smith (1884-1962), was an Australian pianist and harpist, music publisher, and wealthy patron of the arts who founded the music publishing company, Éditions de l’Oiseau-Lyre (Lyrebird Press), in Paris in 1932. (For a fuller account, see JJ to Pound 5 December 1937, notes.)

Pound had asked JJ for help in obtaining from Louise Dyer the Lyrebird Press edition of string sonatas by the English composer, Henry Purcell (1659-1695). (For a fuller account, see JJ to Pound 5 December 1937, notes.)

JJ had sent Pound a copy of the play, Michael Kramer, by the German social realist Gerhart Hauptmann (1862-1946), for Hauptmann to sign. Hauptmann often spent the winter months in Rapallo, where Pound had lived with his wife Dorothy since 1924-1925. (For more details, see JJ to Pound 5 December 1937, notes.)
